capabilities: Plan each week on a board of one to eight named priority cells per day
Drag tasks between cells, days and weeks with a gutter handle
Review the week in a PDCA column (Plan, Do, Check, Act)
Carry unfinished tasks over from the previous week or yesterday
Browse a year overview of ISO weeks with completion-rate fill
disambiguation: Not a calendar or time-blocking scheduler; it plans tasks in named cells per ISO week, with no times of day.
extras: Runs entirely offline with no network requests or telemetry; English and Simplified Chinese are built in, and files keep the language they were written in. Includes a migration command for week files written before year folders.
motivation: The README explains that deciding which of four quadrants a task belongs in "is often more work than the task", so the cells are user-definable (one to eight, named by you).
problem: Obsidian has no built-in weekly planning view, so planning a week in priority quadrants means hand-writing files or leaving Obsidian for a task app.
summary: Weekly planner board that splits each day into named priority cells of Markdown checkbox tasks, with a PDCA review column and a year overview.
